questions.q: When does Li-Ion beat LiPo on board?
options: At T/W above 5 and on short flights
Low current and a long flight
When the peak current is above 10C
questions.explain: Average current per cell ≤ 1.5C and a long flight: Li-Ion gives more Wh/kg but is limited in current.

questions.q: How do you calculate the resistance of a 6S4P pack built from 25 mΩ cells?
questions.explain: Resistances in series add (×S), in parallel they divide (÷P).

questions.q: Why must you not solder to 18650/21700 cells?
questions.explain: Overheating the terminal damages the separator and the protection devices; spot welding heats only the weld spot, for milliseconds.

questions.q: What is wrong with nickel-plated steel strip?
options: It is too expensive for DIY packs
questions.explain: Pure nickel is the standard for current-carrying runs.

questions.q: Why is a classic BMS dangerous in flight?
options: A cutoff in the air means a crash
It is heavy and interferes with the GPS antenna
questions.explain: On flight packs the flight controller does the voltage protection, not a BMS.

questions.q: How do you measure the real capacity of a pack?
options: By a discharge with the current integrated
By the resting voltage an hour after charging
questions.explain: Discharge under load to 3.0 V per cell while integrating the current: only ∫I·dt gives the real delivered capacity.

questions.q: What does an IR difference of > 30% between groups mean?
questions.explain: A bad weld or a bad cell: the high-R group sags first and runs hot.

questions.q: The resistance of a pack built from cells of resistance R:
questions.explain: Resistances in series add and in parallel divide: R·S/P.
